newsitem.title: USA: US FTC seeks to halt Staples/Office Depot merger.
newsitem.headline: US FTC seeks to halt Staples/Office Depot merger.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission made a court filing on Wednesday to halt the merger of Staples Inc and Office Depot Inc, implementing a decision agreed by the commissioners last week.

The FTC asked the federal district court in Washington for a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction to stop the merger from going ahead while the FTC's administrative proceedings against the merger were under way.

Officials at Staples indicated earlier this year that, if the government wins an injunction, the two companies may give up their efforts to merge. Pursuing legal battles has proved costly, and few companies have chosen to fight beyond that point.

If the injunction is denied, Staples and Office Depot would have the right to merge immediately. But it is possible the government could win later on an appeal, which could go as far as the Supreme Court, forcing the merger to stop.

Staples and Office Depot each have about 500 stores. A merged firm would be the largest player in the field, leaving OfficeMax Inc as the next biggest competitor with between 700 and 800 office-supply superstores.
In seeking the restraining order and injunction, the FTC told the court that it would likely succeed in showing that a merger would violate the Clayton antitrust act.
